subject: Security exhibit: scope trade-offs and legal coordination for MSA + Order Form
messages:
From: Sara Hunt <sara.hunt@orchidtx.com>
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: legal@orchidtx.com, procurement@orchidtx.com
Date: 2027-09-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial redlines on security exhibit + schedule

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for sending the MSA and Order Form drafts. We did an internal pass on the security exhibit and attached a marked-up Word with our preferred language. High level items we want to confirm:

- Pen-test window: we prefer an annual pen test with a 30-day notice window.
- Scope: we need SOC 2 evidence for infrastructure and access controls; we also want the right to reasonable inspection (on-site or remote).
- Data retention and deletion clauses: we asked for clarity on logs retention and redaction options.

Can your legal/compliance team weigh in on whether Redwood can commit to a 30-day notice for pen tests and whether the inspection language can be scoped to sampled evidence rather than full access? Procurement is on a condensed timeline, so a reply by EOD Tuesday would help.

I've attached our redline for reference.

Attachment: orchid_security_redlines_v1.docx (docx)

Thanks,
Sara Hunt
Senior Procurement Manager
Orchid Therapeutics

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.com
To: Sara Hunt <sara.hunt@orchidtx.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, olga_petrov@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-19T11:06:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines on security exhibit + schedule

Sara —

Appreciate the quick pass and the file. Looping in Legal (Karthik) and Security (Olga) so we can give concrete answers. Quick thoughts up front so Orchids' procurement team has context:

- Pen-test notice: 30-day notice is workable for scheduled tests; we need a carveout for emergency testing (shorter notice) and for vendor-supplied tooling that requires coordination.
- Inspection scope: we can accept "sampled evidence" approach for operational artifacts and a remote-only inspection model by default to avoid on-site requirements. For very narrow, high-sensitivity requests we can discuss an escalated on-site process.
- SOC 2 evidence: we can provide SOC 2 Type II report and an artifacts list; some infra-level logs are redacted for customer PII/privacy and vendor secrets.

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik to produce a clean redline summarizing the above trade-offs.
2) Olga to propose a pen-test cadence and an ops-friendly evidence cadence spreadsheet.
3) I'll schedule a 30-min legal + security sync with your team Tuesday 10:00 AM PT (please confirm).

If that timeline works I'll attach our proposed language and we can iterate.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: dylan_brooks@redwood.com, Sara Hunt <sara.hunt@orchidtx.com>
Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-20T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines on security exhibit + schedule

Sara, Dylan —

Thanks for the context. I took Orchard's marked-up exhibit and prepared a concise set of redline suggestions (attached). Key items we flagged and rationale:

1) Pen-test notice and window
- We accept a 30-day scheduled notice for non-emergency pen tests.
- We will propose explicit language allowing a shorter notice (72 hours) for vendor-scheduled emergency tests tied to active incidents or critical CVEs where waiting 30 days would pose unacceptable risk.

2) Inspection / audit rights
- We recommend scoped remote-only inspection for SOC-2 artifacts and a mutually-agreed sampling plan for forensic access.
- On-site inspections: we can permit them in narrow circumstances but request that they be limited, scheduled, and conducted under an NDA and documented process (ops runbook).

3) Evidence cadence and log access
- Offer: monthly artifact snapshots (non-PII) + quarterly sampling of raw logs for specified assertions. Full raw log exports that include PII or system secrets will not be delivered; instead we'll provide sanitized extracts and supporting attestations.

4) Contract mechanics
- Suggest an appendix that lists the agreed pen-test calendar, a named ops contact, and an escalation path (CS -> Security -> Legal) to avoid last-minute stalls.

I've attached "security_exhibit_redline_v3.docx" with inline edits and a short comment summary. Olga, can you confirm the technical feasibility of the sampling cadence and propose a pen-test schedule spreadsheet? Marissa — procurement asks for a clear commitable timeline; can you own tracking the agreed dates once they are set?

Attachment: security_exhibit_redline_v3.docx (docx)

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: olga_petrov@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Cc: Sara Hunt <sara.hunt@orchidtx.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-09-22T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial redlines on security exhibit + schedule

All —

Thanks — quick ops confirmation and an attached tentative pen-test cadence workbook (pen-test-schedule.xlsx). Summary:

- Pen-test cadence: annual baseline with optional mid-year vulnerability validation. We can accept 30-day scheduled notice for baseline tests. For critical incident-driven testing we expect to coordinate within 72 hours but will require a prioritized contact list and short runbook to avoid noisy windows.

- Sampling & evidence: implementation proposal below:
  * Monthly sanitized artifact snapshot (config dumps, user-account change logs with PII redacted) — automated, S3 link (read-only).
  * Quarterly sample window where Orchid's security reviewer is granted temporary remote read-only access to a bounded analytics view for 48 hours. Access is ephemeral and logged.
  * For test evidence that requires deeper access (memory snapshots, full flow traces), we require a signed scope amendment and a pre-agreed escalation call.

- On-site: not recommended by default. We'll support on-site only with 60-day advance notice and a mutually-agreed scope; costs/time will be separately scoped.

Action items:
- Dylan: confirm the Tuesday 10am PT sync or propose an alternate.
- Karthik: please add the runbook reference and the language for the scheduled vs. emergency pen-test carveout to the redline.
- Marissa: once Orchid confirms dates, please add the milestones to the procurement tracker and share an invite.

Attachment: pen-test-schedule.xlsx (xlsx)

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Director, Product Security
Redwood Inference
